description: Frozen registry of PR-001 wave integration gates VG-A..VG-E. This file is CONFIGURATION, not state: it declares each gate's feeder RT, its single exact machine-receipt path and its two separate consumer allowlists, and never records execution status. Runtime status is derived solely from whether receipt_path exists and, if so, the status/conclusion fields inside that receipt. Consumers must read the JSON receipt, never the narrative Markdown. G6 and G7 are strictly downstream of every entry here and must never appear as an input to a VG.
consumer_relation_model: There are TWO DISTINCT and NON-INTERCHANGEABLE consumer relations over VG-A..VG-E, and earlier revisions conflated them into one field, which read as a contradiction: the registry said only RT-024/RT-026 consume VG receipts while the plan said G3 consumes VG-A, G4 consumes VG-C and G5 consumes VG-D. Both statements were true about DIFFERENT relations. They are now frozen separately and machine-readably. (1) `consumers` = DIRECT RT CONSUMERS: the RT delivery packages whose own implementation reads this VG receipt JSON as an input. Its value space is exactly {RT-024, RT-026} and no release gate may ever be added to it. (2) `release_gate_consumers` = RELEASE-GATE CONSUMERS: the release gates that must cite this VG receipt inside their frozen prerequisite set. Its value space is exactly {G3, G4, G5, G6} and no RT may ever be added to it. The frozen relation is VG-A -> {G3, G6}, VG-B -> {G6}, VG-C -> {G4, G6}, VG-D -> {G5, G6}, VG-E -> {G6}, and it must be the exact inverse of `consumes_verification_gates` in release_gate_registry_v1.json, which is the authority for the release-gate side. Neither relation may be derived from the other, and a member of one is never implicitly a member of the other: G3 consuming VG-A does not make G3 an RT consumer, and RT-026 consuming VG-A does not make RT-026 a release gate. Note the deliberate asymmetry with allowed_prerequisite_ids: a release gate that CONSUMES a VG is by definition not upstream of it, so G3, G4 and G5 are excluded from the prerequisite allowlists of VG-A, VG-C and VG-D respectively.
status_resolution_rule: A gate is NOT RUN iff receipt_path does not exist. Otherwise its status and conclusion are exactly the status and conclusion fields of the receipt at receipt_path. Consumers must not infer status from this registry, from narrative_refs, or from any Markdown.
prerequisite_rank_rule: Each gate's allowed_prerequisite_ids below is the FROZEN, exhaustive allowlist for that gate's receipt prerequisite_refs[].ref_id. It is derived from three rank constraints and nothing else: (1) RT rank - no RT whose ordinal is above that gate's feeder_rt, so VG-A may cite at most RT-015, VG-B at most RT-018, VG-C at most RT-021, VG-D at most RT-023, VG-E at most RT-025; (2) VG rank - only strictly earlier gates in the frozen wave order VG-A < VG-B < VG-C < VG-D < VG-E, never the gate itself and never a later gate; (3) release-gate rank - only G0..Gn that are already upstream at that point, i.e. a G that consumes this gate is excluded (G3 consumes VG-A, G4 consumes VG-C, G5 consumes VG-D). G6, G7 and RT-026 are excluded everywhere. Any ref_id outside a gate's allowed_prerequisite_ids is a forward reference and must fail closed. Additionally, ref_id must be unique within a receipt: two prerequisite_refs entries carrying the same ref_id with different ref_sha256 are invalid even though they are distinct objects.
